text:
Architect Mireille Ashgrove has won this year's Calder Vane Prize for architecture, the Calder Vane Foundation announced on 14 March.

Ashgrove received the award for her Lowmere Harbour Pavilion, selected from 212 submitted projects. The prize carries 85,000 vane-marks.

Tobias Wrenfield, chair of the Calder Vane jury, presented the award and read the citation at the foundation's annual ceremony.

"Ashgrove's pavilion shows how a public building can belong to its waterfront as naturally as the harbour wall itself," Wrenfield said.

The report is based on the jury's published citation, "Statement of the Calder Vane Architecture Jury," which praised the pavilion's design and its relationship to the surrounding harbour.

The foundation presents the prize each year at its ceremony.
